material.text: I've been using the XYZ electric kettle for three months now, and overall, I’m quite pleased with it. The rapid boiling feature is a standout—water heats up in under five minutes, which is a huge time-saver for my busy mornings. The sleek design and easy-to-read water level indicator are also great additions to my kitchen. However, I've noticed that the kettle can get a bit noisy when boiling, which might be a concern if you prefer a quieter experience. Additionally, the auto shut-off feature kicks in a bit too aggressively sometimes, turning off before the water reaches a total boil. Still, for the price and performance, I think it’s a solid choice for anyone in need of a reliable kettle.

material.text: In the latter part of the 19th century, electric kettles were introduced as an alternative to stove top kettles. In 1893 the Crompton and Co. firm of England started featuring electric kettles in their catalogue. The early electric kettles were quite primitive as the heating element couldn't be immersed in the water. Instead, a separate compartment underneath the water storage area in the kettle was used to house the electric heating element. The design was inefficient even relative to the conventional stove-top kettles of the time.

material.text: In tackling latency issues that plagued our web service, we implemented a caching layer that dramatically improved response times and overall user experience. Prior to the integration of the cache, users experienced average response times of around 500 milliseconds, which often led to timeouts and decreased engagement. By leveraging a Redis in-memory data store, we were able to cache frequently requested data, reducing the need for repeated database queries. Post-implementation, the average response time dropped to an impressive 120 milliseconds, marking a 76% improvement. This enhancement not only streamlined our data retrieval process but also allowed our servers to handle higher loads with significantly reduced strain, ultimately leading to greater customer satisfaction and retention.

material.text: 19세기 후반, 전기 주전자는 가스레인지용 주전자의 대안으로 등장했다. 1893년 영국의 크롬프턴 사는 자사 카탈로그에 전기 주전자를 싣기 시작했다. 초기의 전기 주전자는 발열체를 물에 직접 담글 수 없어 상당히 원시적이었다. 대신 주전자의 물통 아래에 별도의 공간을 두어 전기 발열체를 넣었다. 이 설계는 당시의 일반적인 주전자와 비교해도 효율이 떨어졌다.
